pairs.difference: A (campfire): the logs, stones and kettle are all washed in the same warm glow, and the rocks are soft rounded lumps with no clear core shadow, so the form turn is mushy and the fire acts as a vague ambient source. Form contrast 0.656 is above the real range. B (viewer): there is a clear key light from upper left. The right end-caps and the post's right side fall into a darker blue shadow side, which matches the real cards.
pairs.fix: Light the stones and logs from one side: put a clear dark side on each rock, opposite the fire. Put small, darker contact shadows under every stone. Keep the fire's orange glow to the faces that point at it.

pairs.difference: A (yellow player): the lighting is flat and frontal. The box face is almost one value, with no shadow side on its right flank, and the earbuds and cable are evenly lit. Light bias 0.15 is near the bottom of the real range. B (harmonica): a strong key from the top. The cover plate turns from a bright sheen to a dark lower edge and the front comb face is in shadow, like the directional modeling on the real camera and telescope.
pairs.fix: Light the player from the upper left. Make its right side and bottom edge noticeably darker than the front face, put a soft core shadow where the rounded corners turn away, and put a darker contact shadow under the cable and earbuds.

pairs.difference: A (hat): a clear key from the upper left. The crown's right side turns dark, the brim underside is in deep shadow, and there is a crisp rim along the brim edge, the same pattern as the real cards. B (jacket): the light is mostly frontal on the torso, and the sleeves and pockets get only shallow shading. The dark green vignette and halo behind it supply the drama instead of the jacket's own shadow side.
pairs.fix: Light the jacket from the upper left. Put the right sleeve and the right side of the torso into a clearly darker shadow, put deeper shadows under the collar and the pocket flaps, and keep the bright background glow from replacing shading on the jacket itself.

pairs.difference: A (stage): the coloured spotlights shine from behind, but the pig and the cow are lit flat from the front. The cow's white body has almost no shadow side and no rim from the stage lights. B (farm): warm sun from the right, with shadows under the hat brims and cast shadows on the ground. Both cards sit at the bottom of the real shading range, so this is weak evidence.
pairs.fix: Add coloured rim light from the stage lights along the pig's and the cow's shoulders and ears. Darken the front of their bodies slightly so they read as backlit, with a clear shadow side on the cow's body.

pairs.difference: B (seahorse): shading range 0.51 and form contrast 0.338 are both below the real range. The body ridges have only shallow bands, and there is no clear shadow side on the belly or tail curl, so the light is frontal and even. A (fruit plate): a directional key, with cast shadows from the fruit onto the plate and the plate onto the table, and darker undersides on the grapes and the orange.
pairs.fix: Light the seahorse from the upper left. Make its right side and the underside of the tail curl clearly darker, give each body ridge a dark crease below a lit top edge, and add a faint bright rim along its back.

pairs.difference: A (cactus): a key from the right with a clear core shadow down the left of the trunk and arms, and a long soft cast shadow on the backdrop. B (vending machine): the front face is almost evenly lit and there is only a mild darkening on the left side, so the light is frontal. Both sit inside the real ranges, so this is weak evidence.
pairs.fix: Light the vending machine from the front right. Put the left side panel into a clearly darker shadow, darken the bottom of the cabinet, and draw a soft but darker contact shadow under its feet.

pairs.difference: B (saloon doors): the wood-plank wall is lit flat and evenly from the front, with only weak shading along the door frame. Light bias 0.176 is below the real range. The cast slat shadow on the floor is the only directional cue. A (gate): light from the left, with shadow sides on the brick pillars and the ball finials and directional shadows on the paving.
pairs.fix: Light the scene from one side. Shade the left side of the door frame darker, put a soft darker band where the wall meets the floor, and darken the inside of the doorway.

pairs.difference: B (popcorn cart): frontal, even light. The awning scallops and the cart box are almost the same value across, the wheels have little shadow side, and the contact shadows are weak. A (wagon): a strong key from the right. The canvas top and the box have a clear dark left and under side, and the wheels cast shadows on the dirt, matching the directional modeling on the real cards.
pairs.fix: Light the cart from the upper right. Put the left face of the cart box and the underside of the awning into a clear shadow, shade the inside of the wheels darker, and put dark contact shadows under the wheels on the tiles.

pairs.difference: A (horseshoe): a key from the upper left, with a dark inner right edge and a cast shadow on the wood. B (map and magnifier): the light comes from the upper right, with the magnifier's shadow on the map and the folds shaded. Both have plausible directional modeling inside the real ranges.

A (scarf): form contrast 0.256 is below the real range. The cloth folds turn softly with no deep shadow inside the loop or under the knot, so the scarf reads as evenly lit. B (rope): the coils have clear shadow sides and darker inner loops, and the form contrast is within range.
pairs.fix: Light the scarf from the upper left. Make the inside of the neck loop and the folds under the badge clearly dark, and give each hanging tail a lit front edge and a darker back fold.

pairs.difference: B (towel): shading range 0.494 and form contrast 0.33 are both below the real range. The waves in the cloth are only faint value changes and there is almost no cast shadow under it, so it is flat and frontal. A (target and bear): light from the bulbs above, with the bear's underside and the target's rim in shadow and contact shadows on the shelf.
pairs.fix: Light the towel from the upper left. Give each wave in the cloth a bright crest and a clearly dark trough, and put a soft dark shadow under the lifted corners where they float above the ground.

pairs.difference: B (boots): form contrast 0.383 is below the real range. The leather shafts are evenly lit with only a mild darkening on the right, and the shading is frontal. A (gloves): a strong top-left key, with the right glove's lower half falling into deep shadow and a dark contact shadow on the wood.
pairs.fix: Light the boots from the upper left. Make the right side of each shaft and the back of the heels clearly darker, add a narrow sheen down the lit edge of the leather, and put a dark contact shadow where the soles meet the dirt.

pattern: The generated cards are lit flat and from the front. The lesson pairs show it clearly. On the real camera, monitor and lighthouse, the side turned away from a single key light (upper left or right) drops into a deep shadow and there is a clear core shadow. The generated versions spread light evenly over the front, keep shadow sides shallow, and use halos and background glow instead of modeling the object's own form. The tells are low form contrast and low light bias: undersides and side planes that never go dark, and weak contact shadows.
